title: Add 17-year-old daughter Maya to the Civic (golden demo path)

customer.name: Priya Raman
customer.persona: Working parent calling from home on a weekday evening. Friendly and organized, a little nervous about the price. Your daughter Maya just passed her driving test.

license_status.say_it: her probationary license, she passed last Tuesday

operator_type.say_it: she'll drive it every day to school

coverage_change.say_it: let's keep the limits as they are for now

advice.rep_says: List Maya as the primary driver on the car she will actually drive most; rating her on the wrong car can cause trouble at claim time.
advice.customer_decision: Maya is primary on the 2021 Civic

advice.rep_says: With a B average (3.0 GPA) or better she qualifies for the good-student discount; send a report card within 30 days.
With a new teen driver many families raise liability limits from 50/100 to 100/300; that would add about $11 a month.

talk_track.beat: Greet: your name, the agency, 'this call is recorded for quality and training', ask how you can help.
Say you want to add your daughter to your car insurance; she just got her license.
Congratulate her; ask for the policyholder's name and the policy number so you can pull it up.
Give your name and policy number.
Confirm you found the policy (read back the street address). Ask the daughter's full name and date of birth.
Give Maya's full name (spell the first name) and her date of birth; mention she's 17.
Read the name and date of birth back. Ask which state issued her license, what kind, and any tickets or accidents.
Ohio, probationary license, passed last week, no tickets.
Ask which car she'll drive most and explain why she should be listed as primary on that car. Ask where it's parked overnight.
The Civic, every day to school; it's parked at home (give the ZIP).
Mention the good-student discount (B average or better, report card within 30 days) and suggest raising liability limits for a teen driver (about $11 more a month).
She has a 3.6 GPA. Keep the limits as they are for now.
Ask when Maya should be added to the policy.
Next Friday, October 2nd; that's when she starts driving to school.
Read back: Maya, primary on the Civic, from Friday October 2nd. Quote the new premium ($142 a month, up $46, good-student discount included).
React to the price (a bit much, but OK) and say go ahead.
talk_track.direction: A small 'oof' at the price is perfect.

talk_track.beat: Say they'll hear the assistant in a second, then end the call.

handoff.line: OK if my assistant finishes the paperwork? I'll stay on the line.

rep: This is the call the demo video is built around: relaxed pace, clear numbers.
Say the premium and the date clearly once; don't rush the read-back.
customer: Sound like a real parent; you don't have to use the exact words on the card.

traps: Baseline: every required fact is VERIFIED, so the AI must re-ask nothing (re-asked = 0).
The AI opening should state Maya, the 2021 Civic, Friday October 2, 2026 and $142/month from case state only.
The liability increase was declined; the AI must not re-offer it (that is advice).
